research.finding: One-time key release does not constrain later signatures. The security definition requires extractability. The AADP ciphertext estimate is modeled rather than an end-to-end implementation.
Reports public-ciphertext message-recovery attacks on specified ADP/AADP candidates, including their sparse-circuit regime.
research.disposition: Do not treat that candidate as a secure primitive for this bond.

research.finding: Gives additional polynomial-time cryptanalysis of the ADP candidate.
research.disposition: Candidate-specific cryptanalysis; not an impossibility theorem for all witness encryption.

research.finding: Its standard WE definition protects false instances and explicitly does not promise secrecy on true instances without a witness; the theorem uses fresh random group encodings and oracle access.
research.disposition: Does not establish the extractable, concretely instantiated authorization primitive needed here.

research.finding: Separate publication handles avoid placing all data in the fixed dispute ancestry, but the mismatch instance reverses setup-bound prover/verifier roles; envelope payout details are outside its scope.
research.disposition: Relevant input-publication technique; does not specify our setup-independent challenger admission and fixed collateral payout.

research.finding: Dynamic public scalars use additional blinded garbled computation while a designated verifier still supplies committed labels.
research.disposition: Dynamic input values alone do not establish unknown-challenger admission or authentication of the actual public challenge.

boundaryExperiment.finding: A late-output parent can reuse SINGLE|ANYONECANPAY, but every presigned Taproot child signature mode rejects its changed outpoint.
boundaryExperiment.scope: Rules out the tested naive graft; a different successor/payout construction remains open.

unimplementedFollowup.contestInvariant: An earlier weaker or rebutted candidate must not permanently exclude a timely stronger candidate. Evidence: results/bitvm-fork-contest-model.json; abstract, not Bitcoin enforcement.

subsetPenalty.condition: Nine distinct preimages in one fixed 120-entry bank; disjoint banks and one eight-preimage use per bank.
subsetPenalty.limitation: Not Binohash, a message-binding proof, escrow integration or unknown challenger admission; 208 non-push opcodes exceed the legacy limit.

userDecision.consequence: Do not substitute original-client challenge keys or another trusted online signer.
